 By Fernando Ramirez PUBLISHED: November 5, 2026 at 4:33 PM PST | UPDATED: November 5, 2026 at 6:11 PM PST Getting your Trinity Audio player ready... The San Diego Wave have approached every match since late August with the mentality that each game is a final.
 That message has resonated with both the veterans and younger players on the roster. It helped the Wave win eight of their final 10 matches and remain in contention for the NWSL Shield until the final day of the regular season.
 That mentality has brought them to this point. Just 24 hours before their playoff opener, coach Jonas Eidevall and captain Kenza Dali delivered similar messages to their team.
 “This is what we have fought for,” Eidevall said. “This is what we have trained for, and this is to enjoy the moment. That’s the most important thing that we do tomorrow.”
 “That will be my message is first enjoy it,” Dali said. “We have a lot of players that’s going to be their first playoff game.”
 San Diego will host the Utah Royals in the NWSL playoff quarterfinals Friday night at Snapdragon Stadium.
 This will be the second consecutive year the Wave have reached the playoffs under Eidevall, but this time things are different. Last season, they traveled to Portland for the quarterfinals and were eliminated. This year, San Diego has home-field advantage through the semifinals.
 “Our season is always on the line from this point forward,” defender Kennedy Wesley said.
 Jonas Eidevall of San Diego Wave FC gestures to fans during a Season Kick-Off Rally at Balboa Park on Tuesday, March 10, 2026 in San Diego, California. (Meg McLaughlin / The San Diego Union-Tribune) 
 The Wave have looked like a completely different team in their second season under Eidevall. They have evolved throughout the year, overcoming difficult stretches before finding their rhythm and finishing the regular season strong.
 Star forward Dudinha suffered an injury midway through the season, forcing the Wave to find new scorers. The emergence of Trinity Byars, the maturation of Melanie Barcenas and Gia Corley’s willingness to embrace a new role all helped transform the team.
 San Diego’s style of play also has evolved throughout the season, with the players becoming more comfortable and consistent in executing Eidevall’s system.
 “At the beginning of this year, I think we established, ‘OK, we know what we want things to look like,’” Wesley said. “We know how we want to play, and now it’s a matter of just executing it to the best of our ability and doing it with consistency. I think that’s something that we’ve really seen a lot of this year.”
 Kenza Dali of the San Diego Wave FC celebrates after defeating Portland Thorns FC at Snapdragon Stadium on Wednesday, March 25, 2026 in San Diego, California. (Meg McLaughlin / The San Diego Union-Tribune) 
 Dali has played a significant role in establishing that mentality. As team captain, she commands the attention and respect of everyone in the locker room.
 “I think her leadership has been great,” Wesley said. “Her level of experience is something that not many of us have on this team. So she’s been a really good influence, especially on some of the younger players that are newer to the league, newer to the higher pressure situations and whatnot.”
 Friday night represents exactly what Dali envisioned when she signed with San Diego after spending more than a decade in Europe: an opportunity to compete for a championship, beginning with a home playoff match.
 “It means everything to me,” Dali said, noting that “I came here to win.”
 Considering some of San Diego’s dramatic come-from-behind victories this season, there is a growing sense that this team could be building toward something special.
 The turning point in San Diego’s season came during an August match against the Utah Royals at Snapdragon Stadium. San Diego won 4-2, with Byars scoring twice and Barcenas and Ludmila each adding a goal.
 “I think it really did start to change our momentum a bit,” Wesley explained. “We have obviously been fortunate enough to go into this playoff setting unbeaten in quite a few games, and I do think that that starts with that mentality going into each game, that dropping points isn’t an option anymore. Because if you drop points, you’re done. Your season’s over. So I think we truly have tried to adapt to that, preparing us for this moment on Friday.”
 Second-seeded San Diego enters Friday’s quarterfinal as the team in better form. Seventh-seeded Utah struggled down the stretch, scoring just one goal in its final four matches and failing to win since its Sept. 27 victory over the North Carolina Courage.
 Still, the Royals could present a difficult challenge if they choose to sit deep defensively, limit San Diego’s scoring opportunities and rely on counterattacks.
 That makes discipline and patience especially important for the Wave.
 Fortunately, the Wave have practice. Dali said the key will be trusting the mentality that has brought them this far.
 “It’s just like how you manage the pressure, and I think again, we are built for that,” Dali said. “We have the team for that, and the most important is to truly stick to it.”
 NWSL quarterfinals: No. 2 seed Wave vs. No. 7 seed Utah Royals
 When: 7 p.m. Friday
 Where: Snapdragon Stadium
 TV: Prime Video
